Once set, this bit cannot be cleared, and every subsequent write to this filter entry's FILTER_CONFIG, START_ADDR and END_ADDR registers is steered to the AXI error subordinate and terminates with a DECERR response; reads still return the locked configuration.

ipxact:field.ipxact:name: start_addr
ipxact:field.ipxact:description: Start of the allowable address range, rounded down to the base of its granule. The granule is 4KB when allow_burst is 1, and 2^data_bus_width bytes when allow_burst is 0. Address matching ignores the address bits below the granule, so the accepted range always spans whole granules and is never narrower than one: a range shorter than the granule, start_addr == end_addr included, still admits the whole granule, and two granules if it straddles a granule boundary. Hardware writes the rounded start_addr and end_addr back into these fields only when both land in the same granule; otherwise readback returns the programmed values even though matching is still granule-aligned.

ipxact:field.ipxact:name: end_addr
ipxact:field.ipxact:description: End of the allowable address range, rounded up to the top of its granule. The granule and the write-back behaviour are described under start_addr. Defaults to 7 on reset to match the 8B granule that applies while bursts are disabled.

ipxact:registerFile.ipxact:name: smc_mailbox
ipxact:registerFile.ipxact:displayName: SMC AXI-Lite Mailbox Wrapper Address Map
ipxact:registerFile.ipxact:description: SMC-side wrapper instantiating the AXI-Lite mailbox pairs. Each outbound_mailbox_N / inbound_mailbox_N pair is the two apertures of one bidirectional mailbox and shares a single pair of FIFOs: data written through WRITE_DATA in one aperture is what READ_DATA in the other aperture returns. The outbound/inbound naming reflects intended use, not an access restriction.

ipxact:registerFile.ipxact:name: outbound_mailbox_0
ipxact:registerFile.ipxact:description: Register interface for a single AXI-Lite mailbox: data FIFOs, level and status flags, and interrupt controls.

ipxact:field.ipxact:name: write_data
ipxact:field.ipxact:description: Write data to mailbox fifo. Any write pushes one entry, irrespective of WSTRB, including a write with no byte lanes enabled; byte lanes whose strobe is 0 are pushed as 0.

ipxact:register.ipxact:name: READ_DATA
ipxact:register.ipxact:description: A read of any size or alignment within this register pops one whole 64-bit entry from the mailbox fifo, and only the byte lanes it requests are returned. A 32-bit read of either half therefore discards the other half of the entry; read this register with 64-bit accesses.

ipxact:field.ipxact:name: read_data
ipxact:field.ipxact:description: Read data from mailbox fifo

ipxact:field.ipxact:name: empty
ipxact:field.ipxact:description: 0: Data is available to read, 1: Data is not available to read

ipxact:field.ipxact:name: full
ipxact:field.ipxact:description: 0: Space is available to write, 1: Space is not available to write

ipxact:field.ipxact:name: write_level_above_thresh
ipxact:field.ipxact:description: If set, write fifo level is higher than threshold set in WIRQT

ipxact:field.ipxact:name: read_level_above_thresh
ipxact:field.ipxact:description: If set, read fifo level is higher than threshold set in RIRQT

ipxact:register.ipxact:name: ERROR_FLAGS
ipxact:register.ipxact:description: A read of any size or alignment within this register clears every flag in it. The flags are only returned in the lower 32 bits, so a 32-bit read of the upper half returns 0 and still clears them; read this register with 64-bit accesses or at its lower half.

ipxact:field.ipxact:name: read_error
ipxact:field.ipxact:description: Attempted read from an empty mailbox

ipxact:field.ipxact:name: write_error
ipxact:field.ipxact:description: Attempted write to a full mailbox

ipxact:field.ipxact:name: wirqt
ipxact:field.ipxact:description: When the usage pointer of the FIFO connected to the W channel exceeds this value, a write threshold IRQ is triggered and the corresponding STATUS register bit is set. When a value larger than or equal to the MailboxDepth parameter is written to this register, it gets reduced to MailboxDepth - 1 to ensure an IRQ is triggered when the write FIFO is full.

ipxact:field.ipxact:name: rirqt
ipxact:field.ipxact:description: When the fill pointer of the FIFO connected to the R channel exceeds this value, a read threshold IRQ is triggered and the corresponding STATUS register bit is set. When a value larger than or equal to the MailboxDepth parameter is written to this register, it gets reduced to MailboxDepth - 1 to ensure an IRQ is triggered when the read FIFO is full.

ipxact:register.ipxact:name: IRQS
ipxact:register.ipxact:description: This register is used to read and clear interrupt requests, regardless of IRQEN register and whether the interrupt is enabled or disabled.

ipxact:field.ipxact:name: wtirq
ipxact:field.ipxact:description: On read: [0]: No interrupt request [1]: Usage level threshold in write mailbox exceeded On write: [0]: No acknowledge [1]: Acknowledge and clear interrupt request

ipxact:field.ipxact:name: rtirq
ipxact:field.ipxact:description: On read: [0]: No interrupt request [1]: Usage level threshold in read mailbox exceeded On write: [0]: No acknowledge [1]: Acknowledge and clear interrupt request

ipxact:field.ipxact:name: eirq
ipxact:field.ipxact:description: On read: [0]: No interrupt request [1]: Error on mailbox access On write: [0]: No acknowledge [1]: Acknowledge and clear interrupt request

ipxact:register.ipxact:name: IRQEN
ipxact:register.ipxact:description: This register is used to enable and disable which interrupts are sent to the CPU.

ipxact:field.ipxact:name: wtirq
ipxact:field.ipxact:description: [0]: Write threshold IRQ disabled [1]: Write threshold IRQ enabled

ipxact:field.ipxact:name: rtirq
ipxact:field.ipxact:description: [0]: Read threshold IRQ disabled [1]: Read threshold IRQ enabled

ipxact:field.ipxact:name: eirq
ipxact:field.ipxact:description: [0]: Error IRQ disabled [1]: Error IRQ enabled

ipxact:register.ipxact:description: This register is used to read the current status of the interrupts sent to the CPU.

ipxact:register.ipxact:description: A read of any size or alignment within this register pops one whole 64-bit entry from the mailbox fifo, and only the byte lanes it requests are returned. ipxact:registerFile.ipxact:name: inbound_mailbox_10
ipxact:registerFile.ipxact:description: Register interface for a single AXI-Lite mailbox: data FIFOs, level and status flags, and interrupt controls.

ipxact:field.ipxact:name: write_data
ipxact:field.ipxact:description: Write data to mailbox fifo. Any write pushes one entry, irrespective of WSTRB, including a write with no byte lanes enabled; byte lanes whose strobe is 0 are pushed as 0.

ipxact:register.ipxact:name: READ_DATA
ipxact:register.ipxact:description: A read of any size or alignment within this register pops one whole 64-bit entry from the mailbox fifo, and only the byte lanes it requests are returned. A 32-bit read of either half therefore discards the other half of the entry; read this register with 64-bit accesses.

ipxact:field.ipxact:name: read_data
ipxact:field.ipxact:description: Read data from mailbox fifo

ipxact:field.ipxact:name: empty
ipxact:field.ipxact:description: 0: Data is available to read, 1: Data is not available to read

ipxact:field.ipxact:name: full
ipxact:field.ipxact:description: 0: Space is available to write, 1: Space is not available to write

ipxact:field.ipxact:name: write_level_above_thresh
ipxact:field.ipxact:description: If set, write fifo level is higher than threshold set in WIRQT

ipxact:field.ipxact:name: read_level_above_thresh
ipxact:field.ipxact:description: If set, read fifo level is higher than threshold set in RIRQT

ipxact:register.ipxact:name: ERROR_FLAGS
ipxact:register.ipxact:description: A read of any size or alignment within this register clears every flag in it. The flags are only returned in the lower 32 bits, so a 32-bit read of the upper half returns 0 and still clears them; read this register with 64-bit accesses or at its lower half.

ipxact:field.ipxact:name: read_error
ipxact:field.ipxact:description: Attempted read from an empty mailbox

ipxact:field.ipxact:name: write_error
ipxact:field.ipxact:description: Attempted write to a full mailbox

ipxact:field.ipxact:name: wirqt
ipxact:field.ipxact:description: When the usage pointer of the FIFO connected to the W channel exceeds this value, a write threshold IRQ is triggered and the corresponding STATUS register bit is set. When a value larger than or equal to the MailboxDepth parameter is written to this register, it gets reduced to MailboxDepth - 1 to ensure an IRQ is triggered when the write FIFO is full.

ipxact:field.ipxact:name: rirqt
ipxact:field.ipxact:description: When the fill pointer of the FIFO connected to the R channel exceeds this value, a read threshold IRQ is triggered and the corresponding STATUS register bit is set. When a value larger than or equal to the MailboxDepth parameter is written to this register, it gets reduced to MailboxDepth - 1 to ensure an IRQ is triggered when the read FIFO is full.

ipxact:field.ipxact:name: eirq
ipxact:field.ipxact:description: On read: [0]: No interrupt request [1]: Error on mailbox access On write: [0]: No acknowledge [1]: Acknowledge and clear interrupt request

ipxact:field.ipxact:name: write_data
ipxact:field.ipxact:description: Write data to mailbox fifo. Any write pushes one entry, irrespective of WSTRB, including a write with no byte lanes enabled; byte lanes whose strobe is 0 are pushed as 0.

ipxact:register.ipxact:name: READ_DATA
ipxact:register.ipxact:description: A read of any size or alignment within this register pops one whole 64-bit entry from the mailbox fifo, and only the byte lanes it requests are returned. A 32-bit read of either half therefore discards the other half of the entry; read this register with 64-bit accesses.

ipxact:field.ipxact:name: read_data
ipxact:field.ipxact:description: Read data from mailbox fifo

ipxact:field.ipxact:name: empty
ipxact:field.ipxact:description: 0: Data is available to read, 1: Data is not available to read

ipxact:field.ipxact:name: full
ipxact:field.ipxact:description: 0: Space is available to write, 1: Space is not available to write

ipxact:field.ipxact:name: write_level_above_thresh
ipxact:field.ipxact:description: If set, write fifo level is higher than threshold set in WIRQT

ipxact:field.ipxact:name: read_level_above_thresh
ipxact:field.ipxact:description: If set, read fifo level is higher than threshold set in RIRQT

ipxact:register.ipxact:name: ERROR_FLAGS
ipxact:register.ipxact:description: A read of any size or alignment within this register clears every flag in it. The flags are only returned in the lower 32 bits, so a 32-bit read of the upper half returns 0 and still clears them; read this register with 64-bit accesses or at its lower half.

ipxact:field.ipxact:name: write_error

ipxact:field.ipxact:name: wirqt
ipxact:field.ipxact:description: When the usage pointer of the FIFO connected to the W channel exceeds this value, a write threshold IRQ is triggered and the corresponding STATUS register bit is set. ipxact:field.ipxact:name: write_data
ipxact:field.ipxact:description: Write data to mailbox fifo. Any write pushes one entry, irrespective of WSTRB, including a write with no byte lanes enabled; byte lanes whose strobe is 0 are pushed as 0.

ipxact:register.ipxact:name: READ_DATA
ipxact:register.ipxact:description: A read of any size or alignment within this register pops one whole 64-bit entry from the mailbox fifo, and only the byte lanes it requests are returned. A 32-bit read of either half therefore discards the other half of the entry; read this register with 64-bit accesses.

ipxact:field.ipxact:name: read_data
ipxact:field.ipxact:description: Read data from mailbox fifo

ipxact:field.ipxact:name: empty
ipxact:field.ipxact:description: 0: Data is available to read, 1: Data is not available to read

ipxact:field.ipxact:name: full
ipxact:field.ipxact:description: 0: Space is available to write, 1: Space is not available to write

ipxact:field.ipxact:name: write_level_above_thresh
ipxact:field.ipxact:description: If set, write fifo level is higher than threshold set in WIRQT

ipxact:field.ipxact:name: read_level_above_thresh
ipxact:field.ipxact:description: If set, read fifo level is higher than threshold set in RIRQT

ipxact:register.ipxact:name: ERROR_FLAGS
ipxact:register.ipxact:description: A read of any size or alignment within this register clears every flag in it. The flags are only returned in the lower 32 bits, so a 32-bit read of the upper half returns 0 and still clears them; read this register with 64-bit accesses or at its lower half.

ipxact:field.ipxact:name: read_error
ipxact:field.ipxact:description: Attempted read from an empty mailbox

ipxact:field.ipxact:name: write_error
ipxact:field.ipxact:description: Attempted write to a full mailbox

ipxact:field.ipxact:name: wirqt
ipxact:field.ipxact:description: When the usage pointer of the FIFO connected to the W channel exceeds this value, a write threshold IRQ is triggered and the corresponding STATUS register bit is set. When a value larger than or equal to the MailboxDepth parameter is written to this register, it gets reduced to MailboxDepth - 1 to ensure an IRQ is triggered when the write FIFO is full.

ipxact:field.ipxact:name: rirqt
ipxact:field.ipxact:description: When the fill pointer of the FIFO connected to the R channel exceeds this value, a read threshold IRQ is triggered and the corresponding STATUS register bit is set. When a value larger than or equal to the MailboxDepth parameter is written to this register, it gets reduced to MailboxDepth - 1 to ensure an IRQ is triggered when the read FIFO is full.

ipxact:register.ipxact:name: IRQS
ipxact:register.ipxact:description: This register is used to read and clear interrupt requests, regardless of IRQEN register and whether the interrupt is enabled or disabled.

ipxact:field.ipxact:name: wtirq
ipxact:field.ipxact:description: On read: [0]: No interrupt request [1]: Usage level threshold in write mailbox exceeded On write: [0]: No acknowledge [1]: Acknowledge and clear interrupt request

ipxact:field.ipxact:name: rtirq
ipxact:field.ipxact:description: On read: [0]: No interrupt request [1]: Usage level threshold in read mailbox exceeded On write: [0]: No acknowledge [1]: Acknowledge and clear interrupt request

ipxact:field.ipxact:name: eirq
ipxact:field.ipxact:description: On read: [0]: No interrupt request [1]: Error on mailbox access On write: [0]: No acknowledge [1]: Acknowledge and clear interrupt request

ipxact:register.ipxact:name: IRQEN
ipxact:register.ipxact:description: This register is used to enable and disable which interrupts are sent to the CPU.

ipxact:field.ipxact:name: wtirq
ipxact:field.ipxact:description: [0]: Write threshold IRQ disabled [1]: Write threshold IRQ enabled

ipxact:field.ipxact:name: rtirq
ipxact:field.ipxact:description: [0]: Read threshold IRQ disabled [1]: Read threshold IRQ enabled

ipxact:field.ipxact:name: eirq
ipxact:field.ipxact:description: [0]: Error IRQ disabled [1]: Error IRQ enabled

ipxact:register.ipxact:name: IRQP
ipxact:register.ipxact:description: This register is used to read the current status of the interrupts sent to the CPU.

ipxact:field.ipxact:name: wtirq
ipxact:field.ipxact:description: [0]: No write threshold IRQ pending [1]: Write threshold IRQ pending

ipxact:field.ipxact:name: rtirq
ipxact:field.ipxact:description: [0]: No read threshold IRQ pending [1]: Read threshold IRQ pending

ipxact:field.ipxact:name: eirq
ipxact:field.ipxact:description: [0]: No error IRQ pending [1]: Error IRQ pending

ipxact:field.ipxact:name: wflush
ipxact:field.ipxact:description: Flush the write FIFO for this port

ipxact:field.ipxact:name: rflush
ipxact:field.ipxact:description: Flush the read FIFO for this port

ipxact:field.ipxact:name: write_data
ipxact:field.ipxact:description: Write data to mailbox fifo. Any write pushes one entry, irrespective of WSTRB, including a write with no byte lanes enabled; byte lanes whose strobe is 0 are pushed as 0.

ipxact:register.ipxact:name: READ_DATA
ipxact:register.ipxact:description: A read of any size or alignment within this register pops one whole 64-bit entry from the mailbox fifo, and only the byte lanes it requests are returned. A 32-bit read of either half therefore discards the other half of the entry; read this register with 64-bit accesses.

ipxact:field.ipxact:name: read_data
ipxact:field.ipxact:description: Read data from mailbox fifo

ipxact:field.ipxact:name: full
ipxact:field.ipxact:description: 0: Space is available to write, 1: Space is not available to write

ipxact:field.ipxact:name: write_level_above_thresh
ipxact:field.ipxact:description: If set, write fifo level is higher than threshold set in WIRQT

ipxact:field.ipxact:name: read_level_above_thresh
ipxact:field.ipxact:description: If set, read fifo level is higher than threshold set in RIRQT

ipxact:register.ipxact:name: ERROR_FLAGS
ipxact:register.ipxact:description: A read of any size or alignment within this register clears every flag in it. The flags are only returned in the lower 32 bits, so a 32-bit read of the upper half returns 0 and still clears them; read this register with 64-bit accesses or at its lower half.

ipxact:field.ipxact:name: write_data
ipxact:field.ipxact:description: Write data to mailbox fifo. Any write pushes one entry, irrespective of WSTRB, including a write with no byte lanes enabled; byte lanes whose strobe is 0 are pushed as 0.

ipxact:register.ipxact:name: READ_DATA
ipxact:register.ipxact:description: A read of any size or alignment within this register pops one whole 64-bit entry from the mailbox fifo, and only the byte lanes it requests are returned. A 32-bit read of either half therefore discards the other half of the entry; read this register with 64-bit accesses.

ipxact:field.ipxact:name: read_data
ipxact:field.ipxact:description: Read data from mailbox fifo

ipxact:field.ipxact:name: empty
ipxact:field.ipxact:description: 0: Data is available to read, 1: Data is not available to read

ipxact:field.ipxact:name: full
ipxact:field.ipxact:description: 0: Space is available to write, 1: Space is not available to write

ipxact:field.ipxact:name: write_level_above_thresh
ipxact:field.ipxact:description: If set, write fifo level is higher than threshold set in WIRQT

ipxact:field.ipxact:name: read_level_above_thresh
ipxact:field.ipxact:description: If set, read fifo level is higher than threshold set in RIRQT

ipxact:register.ipxact:name: ERROR_FLAGS
ipxact:register.ipxact:description: A read of any size or alignment within this register clears every flag in it. The flags are only returned in the lower 32 bits, so a 32-bit read of the upper half returns 0 and still clears them; read this register with 64-bit accesses or at its lower half.

ipxact:field.ipxact:name: wirqt
ipxact:field.ipxact:description: When the usage pointer of the FIFO connected to the W channel exceeds this value, a write threshold IRQ is triggered and the corresponding STATUS register bit is set. When a value larger than or equal to the MailboxDepth parameter is written to this register, it gets reduced to MailboxDepth - 1 to ensure an IRQ is triggered when the write FIFO is full.

ipxact:registerFile.ipxact:name: outbound_mailbox_26

ipxact:field.ipxact:name: write_data
ipxact:field.ipxact:description: Write data to mailbox fifo. Any write pushes one entry, irrespective of WSTRB, including a write with no byte lanes enabled; byte lanes whose strobe is 0 are pushed as 0.

ipxact:register.ipxact:name: READ_DATA
ipxact:register.ipxact:description: A read of any size or alignment within this register pops one whole 64-bit entry from the mailbox fifo, and only the byte lanes it requests are returned. A 32-bit read of either half therefore discards the other half of the entry; read this register with 64-bit accesses.

ipxact:field.ipxact:name: read_data
ipxact:field.ipxact:description: Read data from mailbox fifo

ipxact:field.ipxact:name: empty
ipxact:field.ipxact:description: 0: Data is available to read, 1: Data is not available to read

ipxact:field.ipxact:name: full
ipxact:field.ipxact:description: 0: Space is available to write, 1: Space is not available to write

ipxact:field.ipxact:name: write_level_above_thresh
ipxact:field.ipxact:description: If set, write fifo level is higher than threshold set in WIRQT

ipxact:field.ipxact:name: read_level_above_thresh
ipxact:field.ipxact:description: If set, read fifo level is higher than threshold set in RIRQT

ipxact:register.ipxact:name: ERROR_FLAGS
ipxact:register.ipxact:description: A read of any size or alignment within this register clears every flag in it. The flags are only returned in the lower 32 bits, so a 32-bit read of the upper half returns 0 and still clears them; read this register with 64-bit accesses or at its lower half.

ipxact:field.ipxact:name: read_error

ipxact:field.ipxact:name: write_error
ipxact:field.ipxact:description: Attempted write to a full mailbox

ipxact:field.ipxact:name: wirqt
ipxact:field.ipxact:description: When the usage pointer of the FIFO connected to the W channel exceeds this value, a write threshold IRQ is triggered and the corresponding STATUS register bit is set. When a value larger than or equal to the MailboxDepth parameter is written to this register, it gets reduced to MailboxDepth - 1 to ensure an IRQ is triggered when the write FIFO is full.

ipxact:field.ipxact:name: rirqt

ipxact:field.ipxact:name: wtirq
ipxact:field.ipxact:description: On read: [0]: No interrupt request [1]: Usage level threshold in write mailbox exceeded On write: [0]: No acknowledge [1]: Acknowledge and clear interrupt request

ipxact:field.ipxact:description: Write data to mailbox fifo. Any write pushes one entry, irrespective of WSTRB, including a write with no byte lanes enabled; byte lanes whose strobe is 0 are pushed as 0.

ipxact:register.ipxact:name: READ_DATA
ipxact:register.ipxact:description: A read of any size or alignment within this register pops one whole 64-bit entry from the mailbox fifo, and only the byte lanes it requests are returned. A 32-bit read of either half therefore discards the other half of the entry; read this register with 64-bit accesses.

ipxact:field.ipxact:name: read_data
ipxact:field.ipxact:description: Read data from mailbox fifo

ipxact:field.ipxact:name: empty
ipxact:field.ipxact:description: 0: Data is available to read, 1: Data is not available to read

ipxact:field.ipxact:name: full
ipxact:field.ipxact:description: 0: Space is available to write, 1: Space is not available to write

ipxact:field.ipxact:name: write_level_above_thresh
ipxact:field.ipxact:description: If set, write fifo level is higher than threshold set in WIRQT

ipxact:field.ipxact:name: read_level_above_thresh
ipxact:field.ipxact:description: If set, read fifo level is higher than threshold set in RIRQT

ipxact:register.ipxact:name: ERROR_FLAGS
ipxact:register.ipxact:description: A read of any size or alignment within this register clears every flag in it. The flags are only returned in the lower 32 bits, so a 32-bit read of the upper half returns 0 and still clears them; read this register with 64-bit accesses or at its lower half.

ipxact:field.ipxact:name: read_error
ipxact:field.ipxact:description: Attempted read from an empty mailbox

ipxact:field.ipxact:name: write_error
ipxact:field.ipxact:description: Attempted write to a full mailbox

ipxact:field.ipxact:name: wirqt
ipxact:field.ipxact:description: When the usage pointer of the FIFO connected to the W channel exceeds this value, a write threshold IRQ is triggered and the corresponding STATUS register bit is set. When a value larger than or equal to the MailboxDepth parameter is written to this register, it gets reduced to MailboxDepth - 1 to ensure an IRQ is triggered when the write FIFO is full.

ipxact:field.ipxact:name: rirqt
ipxact:field.ipxact:description: When the fill pointer of the FIFO connected to the R channel exceeds this value, a read threshold IRQ is triggered and the corresponding STATUS register bit is set. When a value larger than or equal to the MailboxDepth parameter is written to this register, it gets reduced to MailboxDepth - 1 to ensure an IRQ is triggered when the read FIFO is full.

ipxact:register.ipxact:name: IRQS
ipxact:register.ipxact:description: This register is used to read and clear interrupt requests, regardless of IRQEN register and whether the interrupt is enabled or disabled.

ipxact:field.ipxact:name: wtirq
ipxact:field.ipxact:description: On read: [0]: No interrupt request [1]: Usage level threshold in write mailbox exceeded On write: [0]: No acknowledge [1]: Acknowledge and clear interrupt request

ipxact:field.ipxact:name: rtirq
ipxact:field.ipxact:description: On read: [0]: No interrupt request [1]: Usage level threshold in read mailbox exceeded On write: [0]: No acknowledge [1]: Acknowledge and clear interrupt request

ipxact:field.ipxact:name: eirq
ipxact:field.ipxact:description: On read: [0]: No interrupt request [1]: Error on mailbox access On write: [0]: No acknowledge [1]: Acknowledge and clear interrupt request

ipxact:register.ipxact:name: IRQEN
ipxact:register.ipxact:description: This register is used to enable and disable which interrupts are sent to the CPU.

ipxact:field.ipxact:name: wtirq
ipxact:field.ipxact:description: [0]: Write threshold IRQ disabled [1]: Write threshold IRQ enabled

ipxact:field.ipxact:name: rtirq
ipxact:field.ipxact:description: [0]: Read threshold IRQ disabled [1]: Read threshold IRQ enabled

ipxact:field.ipxact:name: eirq
ipxact:field.ipxact:description: [0]: Error IRQ disabled [1]: Error IRQ enabled

ipxact:register.ipxact:name: IRQP
ipxact:register.ipxact:description: This register is used to read the current status of the interrupts sent to the CPU.

ipxact:field.ipxact:name: wtirq
ipxact:field.ipxact:description: [0]: No write threshold IRQ pending [1]: Write threshold IRQ pending

ipxact:field.ipxact:name: rtirq
ipxact:field.ipxact:description: [0]: No read threshold IRQ pending [1]: Read threshold IRQ pending

ipxact:field.ipxact:name: eirq
ipxact:field.ipxact:description: [0]: No error IRQ pending [1]: Error IRQ pending

ipxact:field.ipxact:name: wflush
ipxact:field.ipxact:description: Flush the write FIFO for this port

ipxact:field.ipxact:name: rflush
ipxact:field.ipxact:description: Flush the read FIFO for this port

ipxact:field.ipxact:name: read_level_above_thresh
ipxact:field.ipxact:description: If set, read fifo level is higher than threshold set in RIRQT

ipxact:register.ipxact:name: ERROR_FLAGS
ipxact:register.ipxact:description: A read of any size or alignment within this register clears every flag in it. The flags are only returned in the lower 32 bits, so a 32-bit read of the upper half returns 0 and still clears them; read this register with 64-bit accesses or at its lower half.

ipxact:field.ipxact:name: read_error
ipxact:field.ipxact:description: Attempted read from an empty mailbox

ipxact:field.ipxact:name: write_error
ipxact:field.ipxact:description: Attempted write to a full mailbox

ipxact:field.ipxact:name: wirqt
ipxact:field.ipxact:description: When the usage pointer of the FIFO connected to the W channel exceeds this value, a write threshold IRQ is triggered and the corresponding STATUS register bit is set. When a value larger than or equal to the MailboxDepth parameter is written to this register, it gets reduced to MailboxDepth - 1 to ensure an IRQ is triggered when the write FIFO is full.

ipxact:field.ipxact:name: rirqt
ipxact:field.ipxact:description: When the fill pointer of the FIFO connected to the R channel exceeds this value, a read threshold IRQ is triggered and the corresponding STATUS register bit is set. When a value larger than or equal to the MailboxDepth parameter is written to this register, it gets reduced to MailboxDepth - 1 to ensure an IRQ is triggered when the read FIFO is full.

ipxact:register.ipxact:name: IRQS
ipxact:register.ipxact:description: This register is used to read and clear interrupt requests, regardless of IRQEN register and whether the interrupt is enabled or disabled.

ipxact:field.ipxact:name: wtirq
ipxact:field.ipxact:description: On read: [0]: No interrupt request [1]: Usage level threshold in write mailbox exceeded On write: [0]: No acknowledge [1]: Acknowledge and clear interrupt request

ipxact:field.ipxact:name: rtirq
ipxact:field.ipxact:description: On read: [0]: No interrupt request [1]: Usage level threshold in read mailbox exceeded On write: [0]: No acknowledge [1]: Acknowledge and clear interrupt request

ipxact:field.ipxact:name: eirq
ipxact:field.ipxact:description: On read: [0]: No interrupt request [1]: Error on mailbox access On write: [0]: No acknowledge [1]: Acknowledge and clear interrupt request

ipxact:register.ipxact:name: IRQEN

ipxact:field.ipxact:name: wtirq
ipxact:field.ipxact:description: [0]: Write threshold IRQ disabled [1]: Write threshold IRQ enabled

ipxact:field.ipxact:name: rtirq

ipxact:field.ipxact:name: eirq

ipxact:register.ipxact:name: IRQP
ipxact:register.ipxact:description: This register is used to read the current status of the interrupts sent to the CPU.

ipxact:field.ipxact:name: wtirq

ipxact:registerFile.ipxact:name: inbound_mailbox_31
ipxact:registerFile.ipxact:description: Register interface for a single AXI-Lite mailbox: data FIFOs, level and status flags, and interrupt controls.

ipxact:field.ipxact:name: write_data
ipxact:field.ipxact:description: Write data to mailbox fifo. Any write pushes one entry, irrespective of WSTRB, including a write with no byte lanes enabled; byte lanes whose strobe is 0 are pushed as 0.

ipxact:register.ipxact:name: READ_DATA
ipxact:register.ipxact:description: A read of any size or alignment within this register pops one whole 64-bit entry from the mailbox fifo, and only the byte lanes it requests are returned. A 32-bit read of either half therefore discards the other half of the entry; read this register with 64-bit accesses.

ipxact:field.ipxact:description: Read data from mailbox fifo

ipxact:field.ipxact:name: full

ipxact:registerFile.ipxact:name: dma_ctrl
ipxact:registerFile.ipxact:description: Source, destination, length, and control registers for the iDMA data-mover engine.

ipxact:field.ipxact:name: DECOUPLE_AW
ipxact:field.ipxact:description: Write-address decoupling. 0: the write address of each burst is held until the first data beat of that burst is ready to be written. 1: write addresses are issued without waiting for write data.

ipxact:field.ipxact:name: DECOUPLE_RW
ipxact:field.ipxact:description: Read/write decoupling. 0: read and write bursts are formed in lockstep, one write burst per read burst. 1: read and write bursts are formed and issued independently; this mode can deadlock.

ipxact:field.ipxact:name: SRC_REDUCE_LEN
ipxact:field.ipxact:description: Source burst-length reduction. 1: read bursts are limited by SRC_MAX_LLEN. 0: a read burst is at most 256 beats and does not cross a 2 KiB-aligned boundary.

ipxact:field.ipxact:name: DST_REDUCE_LEN
ipxact:field.ipxact:description: Destination burst-length reduction. 1: write bursts are limited by DST_MAX_LLEN. 0: a write burst is at most 256 beats and does not cross a 2 KiB-aligned boundary.

ipxact:field.ipxact:name: SRC_MAX_LLEN
ipxact:field.ipxact:description: Base-2 logarithm of the maximum read burst length in 64-bit beats, applied when SRC_REDUCE_LEN is 1. A read burst does not cross a boundary aligned to 2^(SRC_MAX_LLEN+3) bytes; 0 gives single-beat bursts. Ignored when SRC_REDUCE_LEN is 0.

ipxact:field.ipxact:name: DST_MAX_LLEN
ipxact:field.ipxact:description: Base-2 logarithm of the maximum write burst length in 64-bit beats, applied when DST_REDUCE_LEN is 1. A write burst does not cross a boundary aligned to 2^(DST_MAX_LLEN+3) bytes; 0 gives single-beat bursts. Ignored when DST_REDUCE_LEN is 0.

ipxact:field.ipxact:name: ENABLED_ND
ipxact:field.ipxact:description: Repetition enable. 1: the copy is performed NUM_REPETITIONS times, with SRC_STRIDE and DST_STRIDE added to the addresses between rows; set it for every transfer, including a linear copy with NUM_REPETITIONS = 1. 0: the repetition count is forced to zero, so the command completes with an error response, moves no data, and still retires its transfer ID.

ipxact:field.ipxact:name: BUSY
ipxact:field.ipxact:description: Status for the active stream: bits [7:0] each indicate readiness to accept another command, bit 8 indicates midend activity, and bit 9 is zero. These bits do not report backend busy or prove transfer completion; use DONE for completed transfer IDs. Unused streams read zero.

ipxact:field.ipxact:name: DATA
ipxact:field.ipxact:description: Reading this register starts the DMA transfer and returns its transfer ID. IDs start at 2 and skip zero on wrap. The descriptor is not validated: a command with zero repetitions, including one with CONFIG.ENABLED_ND clear, or with a length of 0 still retires an ID without copying any data. A stream bank that is not implemented starts no transfer and returns 0.

ipxact:field.ipxact:description: Size in bytes of zeros to write

ipxact:register.ipxact:name: CTRL_STATUS
ipxact:register.ipxact:description: Any write to this register triggers the start of the zeroer, irrespective of WSTRB, including a write with no byte lanes enabled. The start is ignored while SIZE is 0.

ipxact:field.ipxact:name: INT_EN
ipxact:field.ipxact:description: If enabled, an interrupt will be outputted once zeroer completes.

ipxact:field.ipxact:name: STATUS
ipxact:field.ipxact:description: Indicates whether the zeroer is busy. 1 means the zeroer is active, has pending work, or is in an error state; 0 means it is idle with no pending or outstanding work, including after completion.

ipxact:registerFile.ipxact:name: smc_cpu_ctrl
ipxact:registerFile.ipxact:description: Per-core reset control and status, reset timing, chip configuration, mailbox, and boot-ROM stub registers for the SMC CPU cluster.

ipxact:field.ipxact:name: core0_reset_n_n0_scan
ipxact:field.ipxact:description: Reset control for the CPU, active low.

ipxact:field.ipxact:name: core1_reset_n_n0_scan
ipxact:field.ipxact:description: Reset control for the CPU, active low.

ipxact:field.ipxact:name: core2_reset_n_n0_scan
ipxact:field.ipxact:description: Reset control for the CPU, active low.

ipxact:field.ipxact:name: core3_reset_n_n0_scan
ipxact:field.ipxact:description: Reset control for the CPU, active low.

ipxact:field.ipxact:name: core0_reset_pulse_start_n0_scan
ipxact:field.ipxact:description: Writing a 1 to this register triggers a core reset pulse on core 0, timed by CORE_RESET_PULSE_COUNT. A 0 in core0_reset_n_n0_scan holds the core in reset for the whole pulse.

ipxact:field.ipxact:name: core1_reset_pulse_start_n0_scan
ipxact:field.ipxact:description: Writing a 1 to this register triggers a core reset pulse on core 1, timed by CORE_RESET_PULSE_COUNT. A 0 in core1_reset_n_n0_scan holds the core in reset for the whole pulse.

ipxact:field.ipxact:name: core2_reset_pulse_start_n0_scan
ipxact:field.ipxact:description: Writing a 1 to this register triggers a core reset pulse on core 2, timed by CORE_RESET_PULSE_COUNT. A 0 in core2_reset_n_n0_scan holds the core in reset for the whole pulse.

ipxact:field.ipxact:name: core3_reset_pulse_start_n0_scan
ipxact:field.ipxact:description: Writing a 1 to this register triggers a core reset pulse on core 3, timed by CORE_RESET_PULSE_COUNT. A 0 in core3_reset_n_n0_scan holds the core in reset for the whole pulse.

ipxact:field.ipxact:name: uncore_reset_n_n0_scan
ipxact:field.ipxact:description: Cluster Uncore Reset, active low. Resets the uncore portion of the chipyard cluster and holds every core in reset with it. The reset waits for the cluster boundary to drain, bounded by RESET_TIMEOUT. WARNING: using this can cause any outstanding axi requests to and from the cluster to cause timeouts/exceptions.

ipxact:field.ipxact:name: debug_reset_n_n0_scan
ipxact:field.ipxact:description: Debug Module Reset, active low

ipxact:field.ipxact:name: pre_reset_count
ipxact:field.ipxact:description: Cycles (clk_smc), minus one, from the start of a core reset pulse to reset assertion.

ipxact:field.ipxact:name: post_reset_count
ipxact:field.ipxact:description: Cycles (clk_smc), minus one, that a core reset pulse holds the core in reset.

ipxact:field.ipxact:name: core_resets_done
ipxact:field.ipxact:description: Logic low while performing core reset, logic high otherwise.

ipxact:field.ipxact:name: timeout_value
ipxact:field.ipxact:description: Cycles (clk_smc) a software uncore reset may stay pending (withheld, waiting for drain) before timeout. 0 = disabled, wait indefinitely. Core resets do not wait.

ipxact:field.ipxact:name: timeout_mode
ipxact:field.ipxact:description: Timeout mode: 0 = report the timeout and keep withholding the uncore reset until the drain completes, then apply it; 1 = force the uncore reset on timeout.

ipxact:field.ipxact:name: reset_applied
ipxact:field.ipxact:description: Live status: high while a requested software uncore reset is applied at the cluster, either after drain completes or after a force-mode timeout. Core resets are not reported.

ipxact:field.ipxact:name: reset_timeout
ipxact:field.ipxact:description: Status for the active software uncore reset request: high after the request exceeds timeout_value and remains high until the request is deasserted. Set in both modes.

ipxact:field.ipxact:name: rc
ipxact:field.ipxact:description: Reference counter for the CPU. Write once, then poll this register until the readback reflects the written value before writing again. The counter keeps advancing, so the readback is at or just above the written value rather than equal to it.

ipxact:field.ipxact:name: data
ipxact:field.ipxact:description: Cycle count value that 2nd stage watchdog timer timeout should occur at. Defaults to 16384 cycles

ipxact:field.ipxact:name: reset_cycle_count_0
ipxact:field.ipxact:description: Reset current cycle count value in 2nd stage watchdog timer

ipxact:field.ipxact:name: reset_cycle_count_1
ipxact:field.ipxact:description: Reset current cycle count value in 2nd stage watchdog timer

ipxact:field.ipxact:name: reset_cycle_count_2
ipxact:field.ipxact:description: Reset current cycle count value in 2nd stage watchdog timer

ipxact:field.ipxact:name: reset_cycle_count_3
ipxact:field.ipxact:description: Reset current cycle count value in 2nd stage watchdog timer

ipxact:field.ipxact:name: data
ipxact:field.ipxact:description: Test control register for the CPU

ipxact:field.ipxact:name: data
ipxact:field.ipxact:description: Scratch register for the CPU

ipxact:field.ipxact:name: pc
ipxact:field.ipxact:description: Writeback PC value

ipxact:field.ipxact:name: pc
ipxact:field.ipxact:description: Writeback PC value

ipxact:field.ipxact:name: pc
ipxact:field.ipxact:description: Writeback PC value

ipxact:field.ipxact:name: pc
ipxact:field.ipxact:description: Writeback PC value

ipxact:field.ipxact:name: chiplet_is_primary
ipxact:field.ipxact:description: Indicates if this chiplet is primary (1) or secondary (0). Driven by strap.

ipxact:field.ipxact:name: sram_size
ipxact:field.ipxact:description: Total SRAM size is 2 ^ value bytes

ipxact:register.ipxact:name: MUTEX
ipxact:register.ipxact:description: A read of any size or alignment within this register attempts to acquire the mutex, but the result is only returned in bit 0. A read that does not include byte 0, such as a 32-bit read of the upper half or a byte read at a non-zero offset, returns 0 even when it acquires the mutex, leaving it held with no owner until it is released. Read this register with an access that includes byte 0.

ipxact:field.ipxact:name: mutex
ipxact:field.ipxact:description: HW mutex. Reads will attempt to acquire mutex, 1 on success. If the mutex is already acquired, the read will return 0. To release the mutex, write any value to the register.

ipxact:field.ipxact:name: sema
ipxact:field.ipxact:description: 16-bit semaphore value to inc/dec. Writing to this register will inc/dec the semaphore value. The written value is treated as a signed number using 2s compliment.

ipxact:field.ipxact:name: dummy_rom_word_0
ipxact:field.ipxact:description: Word 0 of WFI loop

ipxact:field.ipxact:name: dummy_rom_word_1
ipxact:field.ipxact:description: Word 1 of WFI loop

ipxact:field.ipxact:name: dummy_rom_word_2
ipxact:field.ipxact:description: Word 2 of WFI loop

ipxact:field.ipxact:name: dummy_rom_word_3

ipxact:field.ipxact:name: dummy_rom_null

ipxact:field.ipxact:description: Enable interrupt when !!INTR_STATE.hci is set.

ipxact:field.ipxact:name: targ
ipxact:field.ipxact:description: Enable interrupt when !!INTR_STATE.targ is set.

ipxact:field.ipxact:name: hci

ipxact:field.ipxact:name: targ

ipxact:field.ipxact:name: fatal_fault

ipxact:field.ipxact:name: regwen

ipxact:field.ipxact:name: REVISION
ipxact:field.ipxact:description: Revision number of the IP block.

ipxact:field.ipxact:name: VERSION
ipxact:field.ipxact:description: Version number of the IP block.

ipxact:field.ipxact:name: DAT_ENTRY_MAX
ipxact:field.ipxact:description: Index of the final entry of the HCI Device Address Table. i.e. one less than the number of entries.

ipxact:field.ipxact:name: DCT_ENTRY_MAX
ipxact:field.ipxact:description: Index of the final entry of the HCI Device Characteristics Table. i.e. one less than the number of entries.

ipxact:field.ipxact:name: BUF_DWORD_MAX
ipxact:field.ipxact:description: Index of the final DWORD of the shared Message Buffer. i.e. one less than its size in DWORDs.

ipxact:field.ipxact:name: PRESENT
ipxact:field.ipxact:description: Indicates the presence of Controller functionality.

ipxact:field.ipxact:name: CE0
ipxact:field.ipxact:description: Count of type 0 Controller Errors.

ipxact:field.ipxact:name: CE1
ipxact:field.ipxact:description: Count of type 1 Controller Errors.

ipxact:field.ipxact:name: CE2
ipxact:field.ipxact:description: Count of type 2 Controller Errors.

ipxact:field.ipxact:name: CE3
ipxact:field.ipxact:description: Count of type 3 Controller Errors.

ipxact:field.ipxact:name: EN
ipxact:field.ipxact:description:
Target enable.
Enable the Target-side logic as a separate I3C device, instead of supporting Standby Controller mode. In this configuration the Controller-side logic must remain the Active Controller and cannot perform Controller Role Handoff.

ipxact:field.ipxact:name: STBY_CR_SUPPORT
ipxact:field.ipxact:description:
Standby Controller role supported.
When set the Controller shall have the option of performing Controller Role Handoff and switching into Standby Controller mode. If this field is clear the Controller will refuse to hand off the bus when requested and will instead remain the Active Controller, thus freeing up the first Virtual Target to operate independently as a dedicated Target device. This version of the IP block does not support Controller Role Handoff.

ipxact:field.ipxact:name: CRHDLY1_AS
ipxact:field.ipxact:description: Controller Handoff Activity State. This information is returned in response to the CRHDLY form of the GETMXDS CCC.

ipxact:field.ipxact:name: CRHDLY1_SET_AS
ipxact:field.ipxact:description: Set Bus Activity State. This information is returned in response to the CRHDLY form of the GETMXDS CCC.

ipxact:field.ipxact:name: EN_HDR_DDR
ipxact:field.ipxact:description:
Declare support for HDR-DDR mode in the GETCAPS response of the Target.
HDR-DDR mode should normally be enabled, and the ability for software to deactivate HDR-DDR mode is included only as a contingency. This configuration bit shall be modified only before the Target is enabled. For the Controller, the issuing of HDR-DDR communications may be avoided in software by the construction of appropriate Command Descriptors.

ipxact:field.ipxact:name: HJ_REQUEST
ipxact:field.ipxact:description:
Issue Hot-Join request.
This applies to all Virtual Targets since they share a single physical Target. Software shall set this to '1' to issue the request, and the hardware will clear it when the request has been sent and acknowledged.

ipxact:field.ipxact:name: SW_RESET
ipxact:field.ipxact:description:
Software reset of Target logic.
Writing '1' to this field will reset all of the Target-side logic and registers. When the Standby Controller is enabled, this will also reset the registers of the Standby Controller, disabling it. To reset only the Standby Controller whilst it is enabled, software should use the `SOFT_RST` field of the HCI-specified `RESET_CONTROL` register instead, to avoid impacting other Virtual Targets.

ipxact:field.ipxact:name: EXT_INFO
ipxact:field.ipxact:description: Extension-specific information.

ipxact:field.ipxact:name: EXT_PRESENT
ipxact:field.ipxact:description:
Indicates whether one or more additional protocols is implemented in the Target hardware.
Some protocols require a sufficiently fast response that software involvement is not possible. These may be implemented as an extension within the Target core.

ipxact:field.ipxact:name: RSTACT
ipxact:field.ipxact:description: Configured Target Reset action.

ipxact:field.ipxact:name: NUM_TARGETS
ipxact:field.ipxact:description: The number of Targets in this implementation.

ipxact:field.ipxact:name: VTM
ipxact:field.ipxact:description: Vendor Test Mode active, in response to ENTTM.

ipxact:field.ipxact:name: PROTOCOL_ERROR
ipxact:field.ipxact:description: Protocol error detected since the last GETSTATUS CCC to read this indicator.

ipxact:field.ipxact:name: CONNECTED
ipxact:field.ipxact:description: Indicates whether the Target logic is connected to the bus and monitoring traffic.

ipxact:field.ipxact:name: ACTIVE
ipxact:field.ipxact:description: Indicates whether the Target logic is presently active, as opposed to under reset.

ipxact:field.ipxact:name: PRESENT
ipxact:field.ipxact:description: Indicates the presence of Target functionality.

ipxact:field.ipxact:name: BUFFER
ipxact:field.ipxact:description:
Specifies the transmission buffer from which DWORDs are to be removed.
0 - IBI Data buffer. 1 - Virtual Target 0 Tx buffer 2 - Virtual Target 1 Tx buffer...

ipxact:field.ipxact:name: LENGTH
ipxact:field.ipxact:description:
Specifies the number of DWORDs to be removed, minus 1.
This field instructs the 'data sink' logic to remove a specified number of DWORDs of data from the specified source. Software shall program 'n-1' into this field to remove 'n' DWORDs.

ipxact:field.ipxact:name: START
ipxact:field.ipxact:description:
Initiate removal of DWORDs from a transmission buffer.
The 'data sink' logic is a mechanism for recovering from aborting or failed transmissions without impacting subsequent, already-queued transfers. Software shall write '1' to this field to start the 'data sink' logic. The ACTIVE field in the corresponding `TARG_SINK_STATUS` register shows whether the logic is still active.

ipxact:field.ipxact:name: ACTIVE
ipxact:field.ipxact:description: Indicates whether the data sink logic is active. This bit becomes set when the operation is started and will be cleared at most a few tens of microseconds later when the operation is complete.

ipxact:field.ipxact:name: ERROR
ipxact:field.ipxact:description: Indicates whether the data sink mechanism stopped prematurely. If the specified buffer did not contain sufficient data for the logic to remove the specified number of DWORDs it will set this bit when becoming inactive.

ipxact:field.ipxact:name: LENGTH
ipxact:field.ipxact:description:
Reports the numbers of DWORDs still to be removed when `ERROR` is asserted.
In the event of an error, this value may be used to ascertain how much of the operation was performed. When this field reports 'm', there are still 'm+1' DWORDs to be removed. In the event of successful completion ('ACTIVE' and 'ERROR' both reset) this field is not meaningful and the DWORDs were removed as expected.

ipxact:field.ipxact:name: SLEEP_REQ
ipxact:field.ipxact:description: Activate the reset detector prior to entry into 'Deepest Sleep' state.

ipxact:field.ipxact:name: WAKE_ACK
ipxact:field.ipxact:description: Wake acknowledgement.

ipxact:field.ipxact:name: RST_PERIPH_EN
ipxact:field.ipxact:description: Enable response to a Peripheral reset request.

ipxact:field.ipxact:name: RST_TARGET_EN
ipxact:field.ipxact:description: Enable response to a Whole Target reset request.

ipxact:field.ipxact:name: ACTIVE
ipxact:field.ipxact:description: Indicates whether the reset detector is active.

ipxact:field.ipxact:name: WAKE_UP
ipxact:field.ipxact:description: Indicates that a Wake Up request was received.

ipxact:field.ipxact:name: RST_PERIPH
ipxact:field.ipxact:description: Indicates that a Peripheral reset request was received.

ipxact:field.ipxact:name: RST_TARGET
ipxact:field.ipxact:description: Indicates that a Whole Target reset request was received.

ipxact:field.ipxact:name: TCBP_DIV2
ipxact:field.ipxact:description: Half of the delay between SCL rising and SDA rising in STOP timing, minus 1. This interval is in terms of the IP clock period. If this field has all bits set then the hardware will calculate a suitable value.

ipxact:field.ipxact:name: TCAS_DIV2
ipxact:field.ipxact:description: Half of the delay between SDA falling and SCL falling in START timing, minus 1. This interval is in terms of the IP clock period. If this field has all bits set then the hardware will calculate a suitable value.

ipxact:field.ipxact:name: SCLLO_DIV2
ipxact:field.ipxact:description: Half of the SCL low interval during Open Drain signaling, minus 1. This interval is in terms of the IP clock period. If this field has all bits set then the hardware will calculate a suitable value.

ipxact:field.ipxact:name: SCLHI_DIV2
ipxact:field.ipxact:description: Half of the SCL high interval during Open Drain signaling, minus 1. This interval is in terms of the IP clock period. If this field has all bits set then the hardware will calculate a suitable value.

ipxact:field.ipxact:name: TCHH
ipxact:field.ipxact:description: Duration of hold phase after rising SCL during Push-Pull signaling, minus 1. This interval is in terms of the IP clock period. If this field has all bits set then the hardware will calculate a suitable value.

ipxact:field.ipxact:name: HCEXT
ipxact:field.ipxact:description: Enable half-cycle SCL extension. If the field `TCHS` has been set to something other than 0x3ff, this bit controls whether the half-cycle SCL extension is enabled. If `TCHS` has all bits set then the hardware will determine this setting automatically. Extending SCL high by half a cycle of the IP clock enables support for other clock frequencies such as 96 MHz.

ipxact:field.ipxact:name: TCHS
ipxact:field.ipxact:description: Duration of setup phase before falling SCL during Push-Pull signaling, minus 1. This interval is in terms of the IP clock period. If this field has all bits set then the hardware will calculate a suitable value.

ipxact:field.ipxact:name: TCLH
ipxact:field.ipxact:description: Duration of hold phase after falling SCL when using Push-Pull signaling at SDR0 rate/HDR-DDR, minus 1. This interval is in terms of the IP clock period. If this field has all bits set then the hardware will calculate a suitable value.

ipxact:field.ipxact:name: TCLS
ipxact:field.ipxact:description: Duration of setup phase before rising SCL when using Push-Pull signaling at SDR0 rate/HDR-DDR, minus 1. This interval is in terms of the IP clock period. If this field has all bits set then the hardware will calculate a suitable value.

ipxact:field.ipxact:name: TCLH
ipxact:field.ipxact:description: Duration of hold phase after falling SCL when using Push-Pull signaling at SDR1 rate, minus 1. This interval is in terms of the IP clock period. If this field has all bits set then the hardware will calculate a suitable value.

ipxact:field.ipxact:name: TCLS
ipxact:field.ipxact:description: Duration of setup phase before rising SCL when using Push-Pull signaling at SDR1 rate, minus 1. This interval is in terms of the IP clock period. If this field has all bits set then the hardware will calculate a suitable value.

ipxact:field.ipxact:name: TCLH
ipxact:field.ipxact:description: Duration of hold phase after falling SCL when using Push-Pull signaling at SDR2 rate, minus 1. This interval is in terms of the IP clock period. If this field has all bits set then the hardware will calculate a suitable value.

ipxact:field.ipxact:name: TCLS
ipxact:field.ipxact:description: Duration of setup phase before rising SCL when using Push-Pull signaling at SDR2, minus 1. This interval is in terms of the IP clock period. If this field has all bits set then the hardware will calculate a suitable value.

ipxact:field.ipxact:name: TCLH
ipxact:field.ipxact:description: Duration of hold phase after falling SCL when using Push-Pull signaling at SDR3 rate, minus 1. This interval is in terms of the IP clock period. If this field has all bits set then the hardware will calculate a suitable value.

ipxact:field.ipxact:name: TCLS
ipxact:field.ipxact:description: Duration of setup phase before rising SCL when using Push-Pull signaling at SDR3 rate, minus 1. This interval is in terms of the IP clock period. If this field has all bits set then the hardware will calculate a suitable value.

ipxact:field.ipxact:name: TCLH
ipxact:field.ipxact:description: Duration of hold phase after falling SCL when using Push-Pull signaling at SDR4 rate, minus 1. This interval is in terms of the IP clock period. If this field has all bits set then the hardware will calculate a suitable value.

ipxact:field.ipxact:name: TCLS
ipxact:field.ipxact:description: Duration of setup phase before rising SCL when using Push-Pull signaling at SDR4 rate, minus 1. This interval is in terms of the IP clock period. If this field has all bits set then the hardware will calculate a suitable value.

ipxact:field.ipxact:name: SCLLO_DIV2
ipxact:field.ipxact:description: Half of the SCL low interval during I2C Fast Mode Plus signaling, minus 1. This interval is in terms of the IP clock period. If this field has all bits set then the hardware will calculate a suitable value.

ipxact:field.ipxact:name: SCLHI_DIV2
ipxact:field.ipxact:description: Half of the SCL high interval during I2C Fast Mode Plus signaling, minus 1. This interval is in terms of the IP clock period. If this field has all bits set then the hardware will calculate a suitable value.

ipxact:field.ipxact:name: SCLLO_DIV2
ipxact:field.ipxact:description: Half of the SCL low interval during I2C Fast Mode signaling, minus 1. This interval is in terms of the IP clock period. If this field has all bits set then the hardware will calculate a suitable value.

ipxact:field.ipxact:name: SCLHI_DIV2
ipxact:field.ipxact:description: Half of the SCL high interval during I2C Fast Mode signaling, minus 1. This interval is in terms of the IP clock period. If this field has all bits set then the hardware will calculate a suitable value.

ipxact:field.ipxact:name: TARG_BUS_AVAIL
ipxact:field.ipxact:description:
Adjustment to the interval of the Target Bus Available timer.
Default interval: 1 microsecond. Base weighting: 1 IP clock cycle.

ipxact:field.ipxact:name: READ_STALLED
ipxact:field.ipxact:description:
Adjustment to the interval of the SDA read stall (no Controller SCL activity during Read Transfer) timer.
Default interval: 150 microseconds. Base weighting: 0x40 IP clock cycles.

ipxact:field.ipxact:name: CTRL_BUS_AVAIL
ipxact:field.ipxact:description:
Adjustment to the interval of the Controller Bus Available timer.
Default interval: 1 microsecond. Base weighting: 1 IP clock cycle.

ipxact:field.ipxact:name: DEAD_BUS
ipxact:field.ipxact:description:
Adjustment to the interval of the Dead Bus timer.
Default interval: 50 milliseconds. Base weighting: 0x4000 IP clock cycles.

ipxact:field.ipxact:name: COMMAND_RETRY
ipxact:field.ipxact:description:
Adjustment to the interval after which NACKed commands are retried.
Default interval: 800 microseconds. Base weighting: 0x100 IP clock cycles.

ipxact:field.ipxact:name: TARG_BUS_IDLE
ipxact:field.ipxact:description:
Adjustment to the interval of the Target Bus Idle timer.
Default interval: 200 microseconds. Base weighting: 0x40 IP clock cycles.

ipxact:field.ipxact:name: TE0_RECOV
ipxact:field.ipxact:description:
Adjustment to the interval after which the Target shall attempt recovery from a Target Error 0 (TE0) condition.
Default interval: 60 microseconds. Base weighting: 0x10 IP clock cycles.

ipxact:field.ipxact:name: TARG_TRX_RST
ipxact:field.ipxact:description:
Adjustment to the Target Reset timer.
Default interval: 5 microseconds. Base weighting: 1 IP clock cycle.

ipxact:field.ipxact:name: SCL_HK_EN
ipxact:field.ipxact:description: High-keeper enable for the SCL line.

ipxact:field.ipxact:name: SDA_HK_EN
ipxact:field.ipxact:description: High-keeper enable for the SDA lane.

ipxact:field.ipxact:name: CTRL_SDA
ipxact:field.ipxact:description: State of the SDA line when direct-driving is enabled.

ipxact:field.ipxact:name: CTRL_SDA_PU_EN
ipxact:field.ipxact:description: Enable pull-up on SDA in direct-driving mode.

ipxact:field.ipxact:name: CTRL_SDA_OD_EN
ipxact:field.ipxact:description: Enable open drain driving of SDA in direct-driving mode.

ipxact:field.ipxact:name: CTRL_SDA_PP_EN
ipxact:field.ipxact:description: Enable push-pull driving of SDA in direct-driving mode, when open drain driving is not also enabled.

ipxact:field.ipxact:name: CTRL_SCL
ipxact:field.ipxact:description: State of the SCL line when direct-driving is enabled.

ipxact:field.ipxact:name: CTRL_SCL_PU_EN
ipxact:field.ipxact:description: Enable pull-up on SCL in direct-driving mode.

ipxact:field.ipxact:name: CTRL_SCL_PP_EN
ipxact:field.ipxact:description: Enable push-pull driving of SCL in direct-driving mode.

ipxact:field.ipxact:name: CTRL_DIRECT_DRIVE_EN
ipxact:field.ipxact:description: Enable direct driving of the Serial Clock (SCL) and Serial Data (SDA) lines by software.

ipxact:field.ipxact:name: ADDR0
ipxact:field.ipxact:description:
First blocked address.
Accesses to the target address (`TARG_ADDR`) will be blocked if the following expression matches: `(TARG_ADDR & MASK0) == ADDR0` The reset values of `MASK0` and `ADDR0` cannot yield a match, deactivating this check.

ipxact:field.ipxact:name: MASK0
ipxact:field.ipxact:description:
Address mask for the first set of blocked addresses.
This mask determines which bits of the device address will be tested and matched against the address in 'ADDR0'. I2C devices are commonly configured with one of a small set of static addresses, differing in only one or two address bits.

ipxact:field.ipxact:name: ADDR1
ipxact:field.ipxact:description:
Second blocked address.
Accesses to the target address (`TARG_ADDR`) will be blocked if the following expression matches: `(TARG_ADDR & MASK1) == ADDR1` The reset values of `MASK1` and `ADDR1` cannot yield a match, deactivating this check.

ipxact:field.ipxact:name: MASK1
ipxact:field.ipxact:description:
Address mask for the second set of blocked addresses.
This mask determines which bits of the device address will be tested and matched against the address in 'ADDR1'. I2C devices are commonly configured with one of a small set of static addresses, differing in only one or two address bits.

ipxact:field.ipxact:name: SW_ADDR_HI
ipxact:field.ipxact:description: Supplies the high address bits when software performs direct accesses to the internal message buffer. The IP may be configured to map part of its internal message buffer into the upper half of the IP address space. This provides more RAM to a memory-limited system when the I3C is not being used, and may be diagnostically useful when it is used. Since half of the IP address space is typically 2 KiB but the message buffer is larger, this field allows software-controlled paging.

ipxact:field.ipxact:name: CLEAR
ipxact:field.ipxact:description: Software clear of buffer state including the following: All `WPTR` and `RPTR` values are set to the corresponding `MIN` values, emptying all circular buffers. This shall only be used when both the Controller- and the Target-side functionality are disabled.

ipxact:field.ipxact:name: TTIQ_ERR
ipxact:field.ipxact:description: Diagnostic error indicator for the Target Transaction Interface (TTI) queues. The hardware sets this bit in the event of a write to a full or read-only queue, or a read from an empty or write-only queue. Software shall clear this bit by writing '1'.

ipxact:field.ipxact:name: HCIQ_ERR
ipxact:field.ipxact:description: Diagnostic error indicator for the Host Controller Interface (HCI) queues. The hardware sets this bit in the event of a write to a full or read-only queue, or a read from an empty or write-only queue. Software shall clear this bit by writing '1'.

ipxact:field.ipxact:name: IBI_SUSPENDED
ipxact:field.ipxact:description: Indicates whether transmission of In-Band Interrupts has been suspended. If an error occurs during transmission, this bit will be set automatically by hardware. Software use of the IBI Abort mechanism described above also causes this bit to become set. It remains asserted until the software writes a 1 to clear this bit.

ipxact:field.ipxact:name: IBI_ABORT
ipxact:field.ipxact:description: Allows software to abort transmission of In-Band Interrupts. Writing 1 to this bit will abort any in-progress IBI transmission. IBI transmission will enter the Suspended stateand will not resume until the Suspended state is cleared.

ipxact:field.ipxact:name: SUSPENDED
ipxact:field.ipxact:description: Indicates, for each Virtual Target in turn, whether transmission has been suspended. If an error occurs during transmission, the corresponding bit will be set automatically by hardware. Software use of the Abort mechanism described above also causes this bit to become set. It remains asserted until the software writes a 1 to clear this bit.

ipxact:field.ipxact:name: ABORT
ipxact:field.ipxact:description: Allows software to abort transmission for each Virtual Target in turn. Writing 1 to the corresponding bit will abort any in-progress transmission from that Virtual Target. Transmission will enter the Suspended state and will not resume until the Suspended state is cleared.

ipxact:registerFile.ipxact:displayName: SMC DFD MMR Aperture Address Map
ipxact:registerFile.ipxact:description: Composite debug (DFD) MMR aperture mapping the DST sink, funnel, CLA, and DST blocks that smc_dfd_wrap instantiates.

ipxact:field.ipxact:name: Trdstramvendorframelength
ipxact:field.ipxact:description: Frame length in 64-byte units. Only 1, 2, 4 and 8 (64, 128, 256 and 512 bytes) are supported, and the value must match the DST's trDstVendorFrameLength.

ipxact:field.ipxact:name: Trdstramrplow
ipxact:field.ipxact:description: Read pointer, in 32-bit words; bits [31:2] of the byte address of the word the next trDstRamData read returns. Each trDstRamData read that returns unread data advances it by one word, and from trDstRamLimitLow it wraps to trDstRamStartLow.

ipxact:field.ipxact:name: Trdstramdata
ipxact:field.ipxact:description: Reading launches a trace-RAM read at trDstRamRPLow. When the RAM holds unread data, the read returns that 32-bit word and advances trDstRamRPLow; otherwise the pointer does not move.

ipxact:field.ipxact:name: PosEdgeSignal0
ipxact:field.ipxact:description: Defines which edge to detect for singal from signal0_select. 1: Pos edge, 0: Neg Edge

ipxact:field.ipxact:name: Signal1Select

ipxact:register.ipxact:name: CDbgEapStatus
ipxact:register.ipxact:description: Register to indicate if an EAP was activated. There is one status bit per EAP in bits [15:0] (Node0Eap0..Node3Eap3, 4 EAPs per Node across 4 Nodes) and one write-to-clear bit per EAP in bits [47:32] (Node0Eap0W2C..Node3Eap3W2C); write the matching w2c bit to reset a status bit. The register is used by SW to know if an action was taken (ex: NMI ISR needs to know which of the EAP triggered the NMI)

ipxact:register.ipxact:name: CDbgClaCtrlStatus
ipxact:register.ipxact:description: Ctrl/Status register to Enable EAP after EAP programming is complete, and read the current node.

ipxact:field.ipxact:name: CurrentNode
ipxact:field.ipxact:description: Read the current node.

ipxact:field.ipxact:name: EnableEap
ipxact:field.ipxact:description: Set Enable EAP to 1 after EAP programming is complete

ipxact:field.ipxact:name: EnableCla
ipxact:field.ipxact:description: Set this bit to 1 to enable the CLA functional clock; clear it to 0 to gate that clock (save pwr). The CLA register block runs on a clock whose functional enable is tied high, so this bit can still be written while the functional clock is gated

ipxact:field.ipxact:name: ClaChainLoopDelay
ipxact:field.ipxact:description: Self-filter delay, in CLA clock cycles, for the CLA's own cross-triggers. When an EAP action drives cross-trigger output n, the CLA ignores incoming cross-trigger n for one cycle, ClaChainLoopDelay cycles later, so that its own trigger returning through the cross-trigger network does not retrigger it; with 0 it ignores the input in the same cycle. A further own trigger while the delay counts does not restart it. Incoming clock halt is not filtered.

ipxact:field.ipxact:name: DisableGlobalClockHalt
ipxact:field.ipxact:description: If this bit is set, clock halt action is not applied to global clocks

ipxact:field.ipxact:name: DisableLocalClockHalt
ipxact:field.ipxact:description: If this bit is set, clock halt action is not applied to local clocks

ipxact:field.ipxact:name: Rsvd6216
ipxact:field.ipxact:description: reserved fields

ipxact:field.ipxact:name: ClaLock
ipxact:field.ipxact:description: If this bit is set, then CLA is locked and the enable_cla is latched forever

ipxact:register.ipxact:name: CDbgMuxSelLo
ipxact:register.ipxact:description: Mode, ID, fine-grain time enable and lane selects for the CLA debug-bus mux, which builds the four 16-bit lanes of the CLA's 64-bit debug bus from 16 input segments. The mux ID is 0: the mode is taken while DbmId is 0, and the lane selects while DbmId is 0 and DbmMode is 1.

ipxact:field.ipxact:name: Dbmmode
ipxact:field.ipxact:description: Mode selection, 0: DBM off, 1: Normal debug mode, 2: DBM ID output mode, 3: Toggle Mode

ipxact:field.ipxact:name: Dbmid
ipxact:field.ipxact:description: Unique DBM ID of the DBM instance

ipxact:field.ipxact:name: Finegraintime
ipxact:field.ipxact:description: Fine Grain Time Enable. If this bit is set, the fine grain time is enabled.

ipxact:field.ipxact:name: Muxselseg0
ipxact:field.ipxact:description: Binary segment select for lane 0 of the CLA debug bus, bits [15:0]. The input segments are 16 bits wide: Seg0 = input bits [15:0], Seg1 = [31:16], and so on to Seg15. 0 selects Seg0; a value k from 1 to 12 selects Seg(k+3), so 1 selects Seg4 and 4 selects Seg7; 13 to 63 drive zero. When FineGrainTime is set, the fine-grain time counter is inserted below Seg0: 0 selects the fine-grain time counter, and k from 1 to 13 selects Seg(k+2).

ipxact:field.ipxact:name: Muxselseg1
ipxact:field.ipxact:description: Binary segment select for lane 1 of the CLA debug bus, bits [31:16]. The input segments are 16 bits wide: Seg0 = input bits [15:0], Seg1 = [31:16], and so on to Seg15. 0 selects Seg1; a value k from 1 to 12 selects Seg(k+3), so 1 selects Seg4 and 4 selects Seg7; 13 to 63 drive zero. When FineGrainTime is set, the fine-grain time counter is inserted below Seg0: 0 selects Seg0, and k from 1 to 13 selects Seg(k+2).

ipxact:field.ipxact:name: Muxselseg2
ipxact:field.ipxact:description: Binary segment select for lane 2 of the CLA debug bus, bits [47:32]. The input segments are 16 bits wide: Seg0 = input bits [15:0], Seg1 = [31:16], and so on to Seg15. 0 selects Seg2; a value k from 1 to 12 selects Seg(k+3), so 1 selects Seg4 and 4 selects Seg7; 13 to 63 drive zero. When FineGrainTime is set, the fine-grain time counter is inserted below Seg0: 0 selects Seg1, and k from 1 to 13 selects Seg(k+2).

ipxact:field.ipxact:name: Muxselseg3
ipxact:field.ipxact:description: Binary segment select for lane 3 of the CLA debug bus, bits [63:48]. The input segments are 16 bits wide: Seg0 = input bits [15:0], Seg1 = [31:16], and so on to Seg15. 0 selects Seg3; a value k from 1 to 12 selects Seg(k+3), so 1 selects Seg4 and 4 selects Seg7; 13 to 63 drive zero. When FineGrainTime is set, the fine-grain time counter is inserted below Seg0: 0 selects Seg2, and k from 1 to 13 selects Seg(k+2).

ipxact:field.ipxact:name: Muxselseg4
ipxact:field.ipxact:description: No effect in the SMC: the CLA debug-bus mux has four output lanes, selected by Muxselseg0 to Muxselseg3.

ipxact:field.ipxact:name: Muxselseg5
ipxact:field.ipxact:description: No effect in the SMC: the CLA debug-bus mux has four output lanes, selected by Muxselseg0 to Muxselseg3.

ipxact:field.ipxact:name: Muxselseg6
ipxact:field.ipxact:description: No effect in the SMC: the CLA debug-bus mux has four output lanes, selected by Muxselseg0 to Muxselseg3.

ipxact:field.ipxact:name: Muxselseg7
ipxact:field.ipxact:description: No effect in the SMC: the CLA debug-bus mux has four output lanes, selected by Muxselseg0 to Muxselseg3.

ipxact:register.ipxact:name: CDbgClaXtriggerTimestretch
ipxact:register.ipxact:description: This value determines the time stretched pulse duration for the cross trigger. 8 bits for each of the two triggers.

ipxact:register.ipxact:name: CDbgClaTimestamp
ipxact:register.ipxact:description: 64-bit timestamp counter. Increments on time_tick. Can be written directly or loaded from timestamp_sync on xtrigger when resync is enabled.

ipxact:field.ipxact:name: TimestampLower
ipxact:field.ipxact:description: Current timestamp value (lower 8 bits)

ipxact:field.ipxact:name: TimestampUpper
ipxact:field.ipxact:description: Current timestamp value (upper 56 bits)

ipxact:register.ipxact:name: CDbgClaTimestampSync
ipxact:register.ipxact:description: Timestamp sync value. This value is loaded into the timestamp register on xtrigger posedge when resync bit is enabled.

ipxact:field.ipxact:name: TimestampSync
ipxact:field.ipxact:description: Sync value to load into timestamp

ipxact:register.ipxact:name: CDbgClaTimestampConfig
ipxact:register.ipxact:description: Timestamp configuration register. Controls resync behavior and debug marker.

ipxact:field.ipxact:name: Resync
ipxact:field.ipxact:description: When set, timestamp is loaded from timestamp_sync on xtrigger posedge. Auto-clears after load.

ipxact:field.ipxact:name: DebugMarker
ipxact:field.ipxact:description: Debug marker output value

ipxact:field.ipxact:name: TsCapture
ipxact:field.ipxact:description: When this bit is set, a cross trigger 0 event will cause the value from Timestamp register to be written into the TimestampCapture register. No effect in the SMC, where the CLA timestamp counts the local time tick (timestamp scheme 0).

ipxact:field.ipxact:name: Rsvd1
ipxact:field.ipxact:description: Reserved

ipxact:register.ipxact:name: CDbgClaTimestampOffset
ipxact:register.ipxact:description: Timestamp offset register. The Offset value is subtracted from the timestamp before comparing with incoming timestamp value. No effect in the SMC, where the CLA timestamp counts the local time tick (timestamp scheme 0).

ipxact:field.ipxact:name: Offset
ipxact:field.ipxact:description: Timestamp offset value. No effect in the SMC.

ipxact:field.ipxact:name: Rsvd0
ipxact:field.ipxact:description: Reserved

ipxact:register.ipxact:name: CDbgSignalMask0Hi
ipxact:register.ipxact:description: Used to define debug bus match events. The positive match event (0x2) fires when debug_bus & mask = match; the negative match event (0x3) fires when debug_bus & mask != match. No effect in the SMC, whose CLA evaluates a 64-bit debug bus; only the Lo register is used.

ipxact:field.ipxact:name: Value
ipxact:field.ipxact:description: Mask to be applied to debug bus before match

ipxact:register.ipxact:name: Scratch
ipxact:register.ipxact:description: Additional scratch register for DV and potential ECO usage

ipxact:field.ipxact:name: Trdstsyncmode
ipxact:field.ipxact:description: Periodic sync mode. 2'b00: off. 2'b01: stream counting, with trDstVendorStreamLength frames between non-compressed packets. 2'b10: send a timestamp packet every 2^(trDstSyncMax + 4) Cluster clocks. 2'b11: no effect, as 2'b00.

ipxact:field.ipxact:name: Trdstsyncmax
ipxact:field.ipxact:description: When trDstSyncMode is set to 2'b10, timestamp will be sent for every 2^(trDstSyncMax + 4) Cluster clocks.

ipxact:field.ipxact:name: Trdstformat
ipxact:field.ipxact:description: bit[0]: XOR Enable, bit[1]: VLT Enable. Supported values : 2'b3 (XOR+VLT Compression), 2'b1 (XOR Compresion), 2'b0 (No Compression)

ipxact:field.ipxact:name: Trdstvendorframelength
ipxact:field.ipxact:description: Specify frame length. Frame Length = trDstVendorFrameLength* 64 bytes; Frame Length should be a multiple of Bank Data Width. Only 1, 2, 4 and 8 (64, 128, 256 and 512 bytes) are supported, because the DST sink finds frame boundaries at the power of two given by the highest set bit of its frame length. Program the sink's trDstRamVendorFrameLength with the same value.

ipxact:field.ipxact:name: Trdstvendorstreamlength
ipxact:field.ipxact:description: Specify Stream length. A stream starts with "no compressed packet". Stream length specifies number of frames before a non-compressed packet is sent, and applies only when trDstSyncMode is 2'b01. Values 0 to 4 give Stream Length = 32* 2^trDstVendorStreamLength (32 to 512 frames); values 5 to 7 give 32.

ipxact:field.ipxact:name: Trdsttimestampconfig
ipxact:field.ipxact:description: DST timestamp configuration. 0: timestamp input form external source (CoreTime). 1: timestamp from CLA timesync.

ipxact:field.ipxact:name: Trdstsrcid
ipxact:field.ipxact:description: Source ID sent in the trace packet headers. Only bits [3:0] are used.

ipxact:field.ipxact:name: TraceSourceId
ipxact:field.ipxact:description: Stored but not used. The trace packet headers carry trDstInstFeatures[trDstSrcID].

ipxact:field.ipxact:name: TraceFrameFillByte
ipxact:field.ipxact:description: Use "Filler Packet" to align a stream of trace packets within a frame boundary.

ipxact:field.ipxact:name: FrameLenghtInBytes
ipxact:field.ipxact:description: Use trDstImpl[trDstVendorFrameLength] for Frame Length programming. Register field ZBB-ed.

ipxact:field.ipxact:name: FrameModeEnable
ipxact:field.ipxact:description: Enable Frame Mode (Frame Mode: Always pack "frame length" number of bytes for trace transmission). If flush to memory is stalled (due to silicon bug), we can have incomplete packets in memory. Frame Mode will help SW decoder to avoid reading incomplete trasnmitted packets. In Frame Mode, SW will get a memory pointer that is aligned to Frame Length. HW will ensure there are no incomplete packets incluced in the region pointed by memory pointer.

ipxact:field.ipxact:name: FrameClosureMode
ipxact:field.ipxact:description: Closure Mode: 1: Close frame with a packet no larger than max packet size before any overflow (due to packets crossing frame boundary). 0: Close frame when packets cross boundary. Push back packet crossing frame boundary to packet generator.

ipxact:register.ipxact:description: Scratch register (high) for DV and potential ECO usage

ipxact:registerFile.ipxact:name: straps
ipxact:registerFile.ipxact:description: Configuration strap values. How they are captured is adopter-defined.

ipxact:field.ipxact:name: straps
ipxact:field.ipxact:description: Configuration straps 0 - 31. Bits 0 - 10, 16, 17, 24 and 27 - 31 have no strap assigned; no strap function consumes them. Strap assignments in this range: * bit 11: CHIP_ID[3] - CHIP_ID is the I2C/I3C static address strap * bit 12: CHIP_ID[2] - CHIP_ID is the I2C/I3C static address strap * bit 13: BYPASS_SRAM_REPAIR - Bypass the memory repair process * bit 14: TEST_EN - Enable DFT test mode * bit 15: CHIP_ID[1] - CHIP_ID is the I2C/I3C static address strap * bit 18: BOOT_I2C - Default alternate boot channel is I3C0 and can be reconfigured to use I2C0 * bit 19: BOOT_RECOVERY - Use I3C0 for BL1 boot image loading instead of the SPI channel * bit 20: BL0_PLLCLK - Use the PLL generated clock by default in BL0, and override to use the reference clock when this strap is asserted * bit 21: STATUS_RPT_DISABLE - Disable BL0 status reporting. It is on by default * bit 22: SPI_USE_FUSED_CONFIG - Use the SPI configuration values stored in the fuse field * bit 23: CHIP_ID[0] - CHIP_ID is the I2C/I3C static address strap * bit 25: PRIMARY_CHIPLET - Identifies the primary chiplet, the boot master * bit 26: SRAM_AUTO_ZERO_DISABLE - Disable auto zero of the SMC SRAM when asserted

ipxact:field.ipxact:name: straps
ipxact:field.ipxact:description: Configuration straps 32 - 60. All bits other than those listed below have no strap assigned; no strap function consumes them. Strap assignments in this range: * bit 22: MBIST_BYPASS - Ignore results of Power-On MBIST for boot * bit 26: ROTATE_UPDATE - Swaps primary and backup image in SEP BL0 ROM
